newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican-Cuba set high-level talks in decades.
newsitem.headline: Dominican-Cuba set high-level talks in decades.

text.p: Dominican officials said on Friday that arrangements were in place for talks next week on a migration agreement with Cuba, the first high-level negotiations between the two Caribbean nations in more than 30 years.

A Cuban delegation headed by Deputy Foreign Minister Maria de los Angeles Flores Paraida was due in Santo Domingo on Sunday for talks beginning on Monday, her Dominican counterpart Minou Tavavez Mirabel said.
Tavavez Mirabal said the talks could be an "important advance" in the process of normalising Dominican-Cuban relations for the first time in three decades.

Hundreds of Cubans have settled in the Dominican Republic after claiming political asylum because they opposed their homeland's Communist government. The Dominican government permitted their entry without granting them formal refugee status or the right to remain for more than three months without making another appeal to remain.
Tavavez Mirabel said the agreement between the two countries would end "the disorder" facing Cuban immigrants, some of whom have had to pay high fees for visas.

During the regime of President Joaquin Balaguer, which ended last summer, a scandal over Cuban visas prompted demonstrations in front of the Dominican consulate in Miami by Cuban-Americans living in that city.
